title: Manage Users and Bootstrap Access
objective: Create repeatable user, group, sudo, and SSH-key bootstrap state.

sourceAlignment.title: Getting started with Ansible 13 - Adding Users & Bootstrapping
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: The user module declares account properties such as name, groups, shell, and presence. Separate key installation and sudo policy into explicit tasks so access decisions remain reviewable.
Bootstrapping solves a transition problem: initial credentials establish the managed account, then automation configures stronger key-based access and removes dependence on the temporary path.
Never put plaintext login or become passwords in a committed inventory. Use Vault or an external credential store, and test the new access path before disabling the old one.
explanation.rule: Create and verify the replacement access path before removing bootstrap credentials.

examples.title: Working design or automation artifact
examples.code:
- name: Create the deploy account
  ansible.builtin.user:
    name: deploy
    groups: sudo
    append: true
    shell: /bin/bash
    state: present
examples.note: Read the structure, predict its effect, then adapt it in the assignment and terminal mission.

assignment.title: Declare a Deploy User
assignment.brief: Create a present deploy account with an explicit shell and supplemental sudo group.
requirements: Include every named safety or behavior requirement.
assignment.solutionCode:
- name: Create the deploy account
  ansible.builtin.user:
    name: deploy
    groups: sudo
    append: true
    shell: /bin/bash
    state: present
